questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes financial management in government as presented in the seminar?
options: The planning, organising, directing and controlling of financial resources to achieve governmental objectives
The collection of taxes and payment of salaries by government agencies
The preparation of annual budgets without responsibility for expenditure control
The supervision of public procurement and auditing to the exclusion of other financial activities
questions.explanation: The seminar defines financial management in government as involving the planning, organising, directing and controlling of financial resources to achieve governmental objectives.

questions.question: Which combination best reflects the processes covered by public financial management in the seminar?
options: Recruitment, staff promotion, establishment control and personnel discipline
Legislative drafting, judicial review, political administration and public relations
Budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, cash/debt management, internal controls and performance measurement
Revenue collection, physical security, document classification and personnel screening
questions.explanation: The introduction identifies budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, cash/debt management, internal controls, performance measurement, policy development and stakeholder engagement as elements of public financial management.

questions.question: Which objective of financial management in government is directly concerned with identifying available government revenue sources and recommending effective collection methods?
options: Safeguarding government assets
Identifying sources of government revenues and recommending effective methods of collection
Evaluating organisational performance in Ministries and Agencies
Preventing reckless spending or over-expenditure
questions.explanation: Identifying sources of government revenue and recommending effective methods of collection is expressly listed as an objective of financial management.

questions.question: A government department manages public funds in a manner that minimises waste while ensuring that resources are used economically, effectively and efficiently in accordance with existing rules. Which objective does this most directly illustrate?
options: Predicting changes in government economic conditions
Enhancing the collection and reporting of public revenue
Optimising the financial benefits of investments
Managing government funds economically, effectively and efficiently in accordance with extant rules
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies economical, effective and efficient management of government funds in accordance with extant rules as one of the objectives.

questions.question: Which objective is most directly concerned with ensuring that public officials can be held answerable for financial decisions and the use of government resources?
options: Promoting accountability and transparency in the government process
Determining and predicting economic conditions
Optimising the benefits of government investment
Recommending methods of revenue collection
questions.explanation: Promoting accountability and transparency is specifically listed among the objectives of financial management in government.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a key component of government financial management rather than merely an objective?
options: Improving citizens' quality of life
Preventing reckless government expenditure
Accounting and reporting
Evaluating organisational performance
questions.explanation: Accounting and reporting is listed among the key components. The other options are objectives of financial management.

questions.question: Which component specifically involves the management process of purchasing goods for government?
options: Debt management
Revenue mobilisation
Financial accounting and reporting
Procurement
questions.explanation: Procurement is identified as the management process of purchasing goods for government.

questions.question: A government entity oversees borrowing arrangements and considers repayment options. Which key component of financial management is being performed?
options: Expenditure management
Debt management
Revenue mobilisation
Financial auditing
questions.explanation: Debt management involves overseeing government borrowings and repayment options.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes expenditure management from revenue mobilisation?
options: Expenditure management concerns government borrowing, while revenue mobilisation concerns financial reporting
Expenditure management concerns auditing, while revenue mobilisation concerns procurement
Expenditure management concerns the efficient use of government funds, while revenue mobilisation concerns collection, borrowing and other sources
Expenditure management concerns investment benefits, while revenue mobilisation concerns internal control alone
questions.explanation: The seminar describes revenue mobilisation as collection, borrowing and other sources, while expenditure management concerns the efficient and effective use of government funds.

questions.question: Which government official submits the budget proposal through an Appropriation Bill to the State House of Assembly and gives assent when the Bill is passed into law, according to the seminar?
options: The Executive Governor
The Commissioner for Finance
The Head of Budget Office
The Accountant-General
questions.explanation: The seminar assigns the submission of the budget proposal through an Appropriation Bill and assent after passage into law to the Executive Governor.

questions.question: Which officer is identified as a member of the State Executive Council responsible for state financing and financial controls through the issuance of regulating instruments known as warrants?
options: The Accountant-General
The State Auditor-General
The Head of Budget Office
The Commissioner for Finance
questions.explanation: The Commissioner for Finance is identified as the State Executive Council member responsible for state financing and financial controls through the issuance of warrants.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the role of the Accountant-General in the seminar?
options: The officer independently audits all public accounts under the Constitution
The officer is the Chief Accounting Officer of the receipts and payment of government funds
The officer exercises legislative oversight over government expenditure
The officer is responsible for budgetary planning on behalf of the State Government
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General is described as the Chief Accounting Officer of the receipts and payment of government funds.

questions.question: A Ministry incurs financial obligations involving both money and materials. Which officer is identified as its Accounting Officer and answerable for those matters?
options: The Permanent Secretary or Head of the Extra-Ministerial Department
The State Auditor-General
The Public Account Committee Chairman
The Revenue Collector
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Departments as Accounting Officers of their Ministries and Departments, answerable for financial matters including manpower and materials.

questions.question: Which responsibility is specifically assigned to the Head of Budget Office?
options: Auditing all public accounts and certifying compliance
Keeping the cash book for the regular collection of revenue
Budgetary planning and control on behalf of the State Government
Issuing payment vouchers and signing cheques on behalf of the Accountant-General
questions.explanation: The Head of Budget Office is responsible for budgetary planning and control on behalf of the State Government.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes the constitutional role of the State Auditor-General in the seminar?
options: The officer controls the issuance of all expenditure warrants
The officer independently audits public accounts to ascertain proper accounting and compliance with rules and regulations
The officer approves the annual budget before it is presented to the House of Assembly
The officer keeps the cash books of revenue collectors and imprest holders
questions.explanation: The State Auditor-General is described as an independent officer responsible under the Constitution for auditing public accounts, checking that monies are fully accounted for and ensuring adequate controls to safeguard government resources.

questions.question: Through which institutional arrangement does the House of Assembly exercise oversight in public financial management, according to the seminar?
options: By issuing warrants to Ministries and Departments
By preparing the financial statements of the State
By maintaining the departmental Vote Book
Through its committee
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the House of Assembly exercises oversight functions in public financial management through its committee.

questions.question: Which body is described as a statutory committee of the State House of Assembly established to examine public accounts and records laid before it by the State Auditor-General?
options: Public Account Committee
State Executive Council
Budget Committee
Procurement Planning Committee
questions.explanation: The Public Account Committee is identified as the statutory committee established to examine public accounts and records laid before it by the State Auditor-General.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a Sub-Accounting Officer?
options: An officer who authorises expenditure on a delegated sub-head through an AIE
An officer entrusted with the regular collection of a particular form of public revenue
An officer entrusted with receipt, custody and disbursement of public money who must keep a recognised cash book
An officer who audits the accounts of public corporations on behalf of the House of Assembly
questions.explanation: A Sub-Accounting Officer is entrusted with receipt, custody and disbursement of public money and is required to keep a recognised cash book.

questions.question: An officer is entrusted with regular collection of a particular form of public revenue and is provided with an official receipt or licence book. Which position does this describe?
options: Imprest Holder
Revenue Collector
Officer Controlling Expenditure
Sub-Accounting Officer
questions.explanation: The Revenue Collector is described as an officer below the Sub-Accounting Officer who collects a particular form of public revenue using an official receipt or licence book and is required to keep a cash book.

questions.question: Which officer is entrusted with control of a sub-head after authority has been delegated by the appropriate accounting officer?
options: Revenue Collector
Imprest Holder
State Auditor-General
Officer Controlling Expenditure
questions.explanation: The Officer Controlling Expenditure is responsible for a sub-head placed under the officer's control by the appropriate accounting officer. The authority is exercised through an Authority to Incur Expenditure.

questions.question: A public officer other than a Sub-Accounting Officer is entrusted with public money for disbursement where the money cannot be expeditiously obtained from a Sub-Accounting Officer. Which position is involved?
options: Revenue Collector
Officer Controlling Expenditure
Imprest Holder
Head of Budget Office
questions.explanation: The seminar defines an Imprest Holder as an officer other than a Sub-Accounting Officer entrusted with public money for disbursement where the money cannot be obtained expeditiously from a Sub-Accounting Officer. The officer must keep a cash book.

questions.question: Which constitutional provision is identified in the seminar as specifying how money should be paid into the Consolidated Revenue Fund and authorising expenditure from it?
options: Sections 120 to 127 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 as amended
Sections 162 to 166 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 as amended
The Finance (Control and Management) Act of 1958
The Audit Law of 2021
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies Sections 120 to 127 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, as specifying how money should be paid into the Consolidated Revenue Fund and authorising expenditure.

questions.question: Which legislation is described as governing the management and operation of all the funds of the government and assigning the Federal Minister of Finance responsibility for government financial business, with corresponding adaptation by the State?
options: The Audit Law of 2021
The Finance (Control and Management) Act of 1958, as amended
The Public Procurement Act of 2007
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Finance (Control and Management) Act of 1958, as amended, as governing the management and operation of government funds and assigning financial responsibilities to the Minister of Finance, with corresponding adaptation by the State.

questions.question: Which regulatory instrument is specifically described as setting out detailed day-to-day rules for collecting, keeping custody of and disbursing government funds in Akwa Ibom State?
options: The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 as amended
The Finance (Control and Management) Act of 1958
The Audit Law of 2021
The Akwa Ibom State Financial Regulation 2009
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Akwa Ibom State Financial Regulation 2009 as setting out detailed rules for the day-to-day collection, custody and disbursement of government funds, including acceptable and non-acceptable practices.

questions.question: A Ministry estimates the revenue it expects to collect within the year through its normal course of activities. Under the seminar's classification, this revenue is best described as:
options: Capital receipts
Recurrent revenue
Development fund revenue
Supplementary revenue
questions.explanation: Recurrent revenue is revenue a Ministry or Department expects to collect within the year in the normal course of its activities.

questions.question: Which combination correctly identifies the two components of recurrent revenue in the seminar?
options: Capital grants and internal loans
Taxes and miscellaneous capital receipts
Statutory allocation and development fund warrants
Internally Generated Revenue and statutory allocation from the Federation Account
questions.explanation: The seminar divides recurrent revenue into Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) and statutory allocation from the Federation Account.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressly identified as a possible source of Internally Generated Revenue?
options: Rent on government property
Development Fund Warrant
Transfer from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for capital projects
Internal and external loans
questions.explanation: The seminar lists taxes, fines and fees, licences, earnings and sales, rent on government property, and dividends and interest on investments as examples of IGR.

questions.question: Under whose oversight function is the State Internal Revenue Service identified as responsible for generating Internally Generated Revenue?
options: The State Auditor-General
The Public Account Committee
The Ministry of Finance
The State House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The seminar places the State Internal Revenue Service under the oversight function of the Ministry of Finance for the generation of IGR.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the Federation Account as presented in the seminar?
options: It is an account exclusively established for capital development expenditure
It is a distributable pool established by Section 162 of the Constitution of Nigeria, 1999, as amended
It is an account maintained exclusively for internally generated revenue
It is a special account used by MDAs to retain unspent recurrent allocations
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Federation Account as a distributable pool established by Section 162 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, as amended.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an exception to the revenue collected by the Federation that is paid into the Federation Account?
options: Value Added Tax
Excess crude revenue
Statutory allocation
Proceeds from PAYE of Armed Forces personnel and other specified federal independent revenue
questions.explanation: The seminar excludes proceeds from PAYE of Armed Forces personnel, police personnel, foreign service officers and residents of the FCT, as well as other Federal Independent Revenue.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations consists of sources of capital receipts rather than the seminar's identified components of recurrent revenue?
options: Grants, internal and external loans, and miscellaneous capital receipts
Taxes, fines, fees and licences
Statutory allocation and rent on government property
Earnings, sales and interest on investments
questions.explanation: Capital receipts include transfers from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for capital projects, grants, internal and external loans, and miscellaneous capital receipts.

questions.question: A government expenditure programme is intended to fund long-term investments in infrastructure from the Capital Development Fund. How does the seminar classify this expenditure?
options: Recurrent expenditure classified by MDA
Recurrent expenditure classified by economic component
Capital expenditure classified according to the relevant sector
Statutory recurrent expenditure classified by revenue source
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure involves disbursements from the Capital Development Fund for government investments in infrastructure and long-term development plans. The seminar identifies sectors such as Administrative, Economic, Social, Law and Justice, and Regional.

questions.question: Which combination most accurately describes recurrent expenditure under the seminar?
options: Long-term infrastructure investments financed exclusively from development grants
Annual administrative costs, including personal emoluments, administrative overheads and Consolidated Revenue Fund charges
Capital projects classified into Administrative, Economic and Social sectors
Loans and grants transferred to government from external sources
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure is largely incurred to meet the annual cost of administration and includes personal emoluments, administrative overheads and Consolidated Revenue Fund charges, including loan-servicing costs.

questions.question: A government department incurs expenditure that was not provided for in the year's Appropriation Law and subsequently exceeds its approved expenditure provision. Which statement best reflects the seminar's position?
options: The expenditure is permitted if the Permanent Secretary approves it
The expenditure is acceptable if it relates to administrative overheads
The expenditure becomes lawful once it is entered in the Cash Book
Unbudgeted expenditure is not allowed with public funds, and over-expenditure constitutes a punishable offence
questions.explanation: The seminar states that all types of expenditure must be provided for in the Appropriation Law of the year. Unbudgeted expenditure is not allowed, and over-expenditure constitutes a punishable offence.

questions.question: A Revenue Collector issues an official receipt for funds received but fails to enter the receipt in the cash book. The corresponding value is also yet to be confirmed through a bank statement. Under the seminar, how should the revenue be treated?
options: It has not yet satisfied all the conditions for being accounted for
It is fully accounted for once the official receipt is issued
It is accounted for once the Revenue Collector reports the amount verbally
It becomes accounted for when the funds are entered in the departmental Vote Book
questions.explanation: Revenue is not accounted for until the Revenue Collector's receipt has been issued, the receipts are entered in the Revenue Collector's Cash Book, and the value is confirmed through a bank statement. All three conditions matter.

questions.question: A Revenue Collector receives government revenue in cash and wishes to use part of it to settle an immediate departmental expense before lodging the balance. Which response is consistent with the seminar?
options: The Revenue Collector may retain the cash for up to seven days if the expense is official
The Revenue Collector may disburse the money after obtaining verbal approval from the Permanent Secretary
Cash payment is strongly discouraged, revenue should not remain unlodged beyond 48 hours, and disbursement requires express authorisation from the State Accountant-General
The Revenue Collector may use the money if the transaction is entered in the Cash Book
questions.explanation: The seminar strongly discourages cash payment of revenue, states there is no acceptable reason for failing to lodge revenue within 48 hours, and prohibits disbursement from collected revenue without express authorisation from the State Accountant-General.

questions.question: Following enactment of the Appropriation Law, which arrangement authorises funds to be made available to MDAs for spending in accordance with the approved budget?
options: The State Auditor-General issues instructions directly to every MDA
The Commissioner for Finance issues a warrant authorising the Accountant-General to make funds available
The Head of Budget Office releases funds directly to Revenue Collectors
The Public Account Committee issues payment vouchers to the Treasury
questions.explanation: After enactment of the Appropriation Law, the Commissioner for Finance authorises the Accountant-General through a warrant to make funds available to MDAs in accordance with the budget.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly identified as a type of Recurrent Expenditure Warrant?
options: Development Fund Special Warrant
Provisional Development Fund Warrant
Development Fund Reserved Warrant
Supplementary General Warrant
questions.explanation: Supplementary General Warrant is among the recurrent expenditure warrants listed in the seminar under FR 402–408.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the category of Capital Expenditure Warrants?
options: Development Fund Special Warrant
Annual General Warrant
Reserved Expenditure Warrant
Supplementary Contingencies Warrant
questions.explanation: Development Fund Special Warrant is listed among the capital expenditure warrants under FR 416–424.

questions.question: A Ministry proposes using a Virement Warrant to move funds between expenditure provisions. Which condition must be observed under the seminar?
options: Approval may be granted by the Revenue Collector where the expenditure is urgent
The warrant can be used without approval if the Ministry has sufficient total allocation
Approval must be obtained from the House of Assembly, and sufficient money must exist in the vote within the same economic component
Approval is required only from the Internal Audit Unit
questions.explanation: The seminar states that Virement Warrant is no longer in use. If it must be used, House of Assembly approval is required, and sufficient money must be available in the vote within the same economic component.

questions.question: Which statement correctly reflects the initial requirements for government disbursement under the seminar's payment procedure?
options: All payments must first be recorded in the Cash Book before a payment voucher is prepared
All disbursements must be made through payment vouchers, which should also be entered in the Vote Book and Cash Book
All payments may be made through bank transfers without payment vouchers
Payment vouchers are only necessary for capital expenditure
questions.explanation: The seminar requires all disbursements to be made through Payment Vouchers (PVs). The vouchers should also be entered in the Vote Book and Cash Book.

questions.question: A payment voucher has been prepared and entered in the relevant books. What is the next review arrangement specified in the seminar?
options: It must be forwarded directly to the payee for collection
It must be sent to the State Auditor-General for final approval
It must be sent to the Public Account Committee for authorisation
It must be sent to the Ministry or Department's Internal Audit Unit for vetting and review, after which an authorised officer signs to confirm its correctness
questions.explanation: The seminar directs that the payment voucher be sent to the Internal Audit Unit for vetting and review. After the review, a duly authorised officer signs to vouch that the information is correct and consistent with the Financial Regulations.

questions.question: After the Internal Audit Unit has reviewed a payment voucher and the required authorised officer has signed it, which route should it follow?
options: Submission through a Payment Vouchers Schedule to the Treasury for payment
Submission directly to the State House of Assembly for approval
Return to the Revenue Collector for cash disbursement
Forwarding to the Public Account Committee for certification
questions.explanation: The seminar requires the voucher to be submitted through a Payment Vouchers Schedule to the Treasury. The Treasury then checks and verifies the voucher before passing it for payment.

questions.question: A cheque has been issued following certification of a payment. Which action must the payee take before collecting it under the procedure described in the seminar?
options: Obtain a new warrant from the Commissioner for Finance
Secure approval from the Public Account Committee
Provide proper identification and sign the paid voucher and cheque register
Prepare a new payment voucher and submit it to Internal Audit
questions.explanation: After certification, a cheque is issued to the payee. Following proper identification, the payee signs the paid voucher and cheque register before collecting the cheque.

questions.question: Under Financial Regulation FR 804, which arrangement is required for cheques drawn against an official bank account?
options: They may be signed by one Sub-Accounting Officer and a Revenue Collector
They must be signed by two officers: the Accounting Officer and another officer not below Senior Executive Officer, GL 09
They must be signed by the Commissioner for Finance and the State Auditor-General
They may be signed by any two officers authorised by the Head of Budget Office
questions.explanation: FR 804 requires two signatories: the Accounting Officer and another officer not below the rank of Senior Executive Officer, GL 09.

questions.question: Which statement correctly reflects the seminar's provisions on banking facilities and electronic payment?
options: FR 901 permits cash to replace banking facilities, while e-payment applies only to payments below ₦10 million
FR 901 concerns cheque signatories, while payments above ₦20,000 must be made electronically
FR 901 requires agencies to retain substantial office cash, while e-payment applies only to capital expenditure

FR 901 requires government agencies to make full use of banking facilities, while the seminar states that under the e-payment system, any amount from ₦10 million must be paid electronically into the authorised account of the payee
questions.explanation: FR 901 states that government agencies should make full use of banking facilities. Separately, the seminar states that under the e-payment system, any amount from ₦10 million must be paid electronically into the authorised account of the payee.

questions.question: A government agency is making several small payments and one payment of ₦15,000. What does FR 809, as presented in the seminar, require?
options: Only sufficient cash for small payments should be kept in the office; payments above ₦10,000 should be made through cheques and transfers
All payments should be made in cash if they are below ₦20,000
Payments above ₦10,000 may be made in cash if approved by the Revenue Collector
All small payments must be made through cheques, while payments above ₦10,000 may be made in cash
questions.explanation: FR 809 provides that only sufficient cash to meet small payments should be kept in the office, while payments above ₦10,000 should be made through cheques and transfers.

questions.question: Which option correctly pairs the two Financial Regulation provisions concerning bank reconciliation and imprest?
options: FR 811 requires imprest through a bank account above ₦20,000; FR 1109 requires monthly reconciliation only
FR 811 concerns cheque signatories; FR 1109 concerns the use of banking facilities
FR 811 requires weekly/monthly reconciliation between the Cash Book and Bank Statements; FR 1109 states that imprest should be made through a bank account above ₦20,000
FR 811 prohibits cash payments above ₦10,000; FR 1109 requires two officers to sign every cheque
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies FR 811 with weekly/monthly reconciliation between the Cash Book and Bank Statements, while FR 1109 stipulates that imprest should be made through a bank account above ₦20,000.

questions.question: A payment voucher is being prepared for processing in a government department. Which requirement concerning the number of copies is expressly stated in the seminar?
options: At least two copies per set
At least three copies per set
At least five copies per set
At least six copies per set
questions.explanation: The seminar specifies that payment vouchers should be kept and used in at least five copies per set.

questions.question: An accounting office wants to maintain a record that assigns serial numbers to payment vouchers. Which document is specifically intended for this purpose?
options: Payment Voucher Register
Payment Voucher Schedule
Cheques/Cash Payment Register
Departmental Vote Book
questions.explanation: The Payment Voucher Register is maintained for the serial numbering of payment vouchers. The Payment Voucher Schedule serves a different purpose: forwarding payment vouchers.

questions.question: Which document is specifically identified as the instrument used to forward payment vouchers?
options: File copy of the voucher
Cash Book
Payment Voucher Register
Payment Voucher Schedule
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the Payment Voucher Schedule as the document used to forward payment vouchers.

questions.question: During a financial records inspection, an auditor asks to see the documentary basis for the approved budget against which payments are being processed. Which item in the seminar's required payment records is most directly relevant?
options: Revenue Collector's official receipt book
A copy of the approved budget or an extract thereof
The personal cash book of the Imprest Holder
The procurement bid evaluation report
questions.explanation: A copy of the approved budget or an extract thereof is expressly included among the documents required to be kept and used in payments.

questions.question: Which description best captures the primary function of the Departmental Vote Book?
options: It records revenue collected from all government sources
It lists all payment vouchers awaiting Treasury approval
It shows the budgeted amount, expenditure, cumulative expenditure and unexpended balance on sub-heads
It records only the final balances of departmental bank accounts
questions.explanation: The Departmental Vote Book shows the budgeted amount, expenditure, cumulative expenditure and unexpended balance on sub-heads from time to time. It is an important expenditure-control record.

questions.question: Why does the seminar regard the Departmental Vote Book as an integral part of the public-sector accounting control system?
options: It determines which Ministries may generate internally generated revenue
It replaces the need for the approved budget
It authorises the Treasury to issue cheques without supporting documents
It helps the Accounting Officer guard against over-expenditure
questions.explanation: The seminar explains that the Vote Book helps the Accounting Officer guard against over-expenditure by providing an ongoing record of expenditure against budgetary provisions.

questions.question: For every item of expenditure posted in the Departmental Vote Book, whose signature is required against the entry according to the seminar?
options: The Accounting Officer, identified as the Permanent Secretary
The Revenue Collector
The State Auditor-General
The Chairman of the Public Account Committee
questions.explanation: The seminar states that for every item of expenditure posted, the Accounting Officer (Permanent Secretary) must sign against it.

questions.question: Under Chapter 5 of the Revised Financial Regulation, what is the responsibility of the Accounting Officer concerning the Departmental Vote Book?
options: To approve every revenue collection before it is banked
To monitor departmental expenditure against the amount provided in the estimates and keep the Vote Book up to date
To conduct the external audit of all departmental accounts
To prepare the State's consolidated financial statements
questions.explanation: Chapter 5 places responsibility on the Accounting Officer to watch expenditure against the amounts provided in the estimates and ensure that the Vote Book is posted up to date.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the details the seminar says should be indicated in the Departmental Vote Book?
options: The head or sub-head of expenditure
The amount approved in the estimates
The departmental payment voucher number
The personal bank account number of the officer receiving payment
questions.explanation: The Vote Book should contain expenditure-related information such as the head or sub-head, description, approved amount, revisions, expenditure, payment voucher number, cumulative payments, liabilities and available balance. The payee's personal bank account number is not among the listed details.

questions.question: A departmental Vote Book shows the amount approved in the estimates and the expenditure incurred, but it fails to reflect any known liabilities under the relevant sub-head. Which required entry is missing?
options: Any known liabilities under the sub-head
The date of the next budget briefing
The name of the officer who prepared the annual budget
The amount of revenue generated by other Ministries
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically requires the Vote Book to indicate any known liabilities under the sub-head, in addition to the budgetary and expenditure details.

questions.question: A payment voucher has been prepared and checked, but the expenditure has not been posted into the Departmental Vote Book. What does the seminar say about processing such a voucher?
options: It may be processed if the Treasury has sufficient cash
It is irregular to process a payment voucher that has not been posted into the Vote Book
It may be processed if the Revenue Collector signs it
It should be processed first and entered into the Vote Book at the end of the month
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that it is irregular to process a payment voucher which has not been posted into the Vote Book.

questions.question: Which action provides evidence that a payment voucher has been entered into the Departmental Vote Book?
options: Affixing the usual 'Entered into Vote Book' stamp, together with initials and date
Attaching a copy of the payee's identification card
Obtaining a fresh warrant from the Commissioner for Finance
Recording the voucher only in the Cheques/Cash Payment Register
questions.explanation: The seminar states that a stamp bearing 'Entered into Vote Book' is usually used, together with the initials and date, to indicate that the action has been taken.

questions.question: An Accounting Officer wishes to delegate the day-to-day control of departmental expenditure to a subordinate officer. Which arrangement is consistent with the seminar?
options: Oral permission from the Head of Budget Office
Automatic delegation to the Revenue Collector
Written instruction delegating the responsibility, after which the subordinate keeps the Vote Book
Approval from the Public Account Committee without any written instruction
questions.explanation: The seminar allows the Accounting Officer to delegate day-to-day expenditure control to a subordinate through written instruction. The delegated officer then keeps the Vote Book.

questions.question: Under what circumstances does the seminar say an Accounting Officer may use an Authority to Incur Expenditure?
options: When transferring revenue between the Federation Account and the Consolidated Revenue Fund
When authorising another officer to incur expenditure and sign vouchers on the Accounting Officer's behalf
When authorising the State Auditor-General to examine the departmental accounts
When permitting a Revenue Collector to retain government revenue beyond the normal lodging period
questions.explanation: An AIE is used where the Accounting Officer needs to authorise other officers to incur expenditure and sign vouchers on the Accounting Officer's behalf.

questions.question: Which institution is identified as the usual issuing authority for an Authority to Incur Expenditure?
options: The State Auditor-General's Office
The Ministry of Justice
The Office of the Accountant-General alone
The State Budget Office
questions.explanation: The seminar states that an Authority to Incur Expenditure is usually issued by the State Budget Office.

questions.question: Which description best captures a government budget as defined in the seminar?
options: A record of revenue already collected and expenditure already incurred
A plan dealing exclusively with capital projects
A quantitative plan of action and authorised forecast of anticipated government revenue and expenditure for a defined period
A legislative document listing only the financial entitlements of public servants
questions.explanation: The seminar describes a budget as a quantitative plan of action that aids coordination and implementation of government plans, and as an authorised forecast of anticipated revenue and expenditure for a defined period.

questions.question: Which combination represents the three components of the State Government budget listed in the seminar?
options: Recurrent revenue, capital receipts and statutory allocation
Personnel Cost, Overhead Cost and Capital Budget
Recurrent expenditure, debt servicing and procurement expenditure
Personnel Cost, statutory allocation and development grants
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies Personnel Cost, Overhead Cost and Capital Budget as the components of the State budget.

questions.question: A government department uses the budget to establish the maximum expenditure it may incur within a defined period. Which budget purpose does this illustrate?
options: Providing a basis for determining staff promotions
Identifying officers responsible for internal audit
Regulating revenue collection methods
Stipulating expenditure limits within the period
questions.explanation: One of the purposes of a budget identified in the seminar is to stipulate expenditure limits within the period covered.

questions.question: Which budgetary function is most directly illustrated when government uses the budget to determine how limited public funds are distributed among competing programmes?
options: Showing how scarce resources are distributed
Establishing the hierarchy of financial officers
Determining how payment vouchers are numbered
Identifying the statutory classification of public revenue
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the distribution of scarce resources as one of the purposes of the government budget.

questions.question: A Ministry is preparing proposals for the next financial year. Which institution is identified as having oversight of the process of gathering quantitative forecasts from individual Ministries, Departments and Agencies?
options: Public Account Committee
State Auditor-General's Office
State Budget Office
Office of the Commissioner for Finance alone
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the State Budget Office has oversight of gathering forecasts from individual Ministries, Departments and Agencies.

questions.question: Which action initiates the government budget development process described in the seminar?
options: Presentation of the final Draft Budget to the House of Assembly
Issuance of call circulars by the Head of Budget Office inviting MDA proposals for the coming year
Conduct of public budget hearings by the House of Assembly
Preparation of the final executive brief by the Governor
questions.explanation: The first stage identified is the issuance of call circulars by the Head of Budget Office, inviting MDAs to submit proposals for the coming year.

questions.question: After call circulars have been issued, who is responsible for constituting budget committees within the Ministries, Departments and Agencies?
options: The State Auditor-General
The Commissioner for Finance
The Public Account Committee
The Permanent Secretary or Head of the Extra-Ministerial Department
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Permanent Secretary or Head of an Extra-Ministerial Department constitutes budget committees for the respective MDAs.

questions.question: Following the constitution of MDA budget committees, what happens to the quantitative forecasts prepared by the Ministries, Departments and Agencies?
options: They are returned to the budgeting authorities, after which the respective MDAs meet to discuss or substantiate their estimates
They are immediately passed into law by the House of Assembly
They are sent directly to the Auditor-General for certification
They are published for public review before being submitted to the State Budget Office
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the return of forecasts to the budgeting authorities, followed by meetings between the respective MDAs and the authorities to discuss or substantiate their estimates.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the later stages of the government budget process after the MDA estimates have been discussed and substantiated?
options: Public briefing, call circulars, budget committee formation, then preparation of the draft estimates
Appropriation Bill, MDA forecasts, State Executive Council review, then budget call circulars

Budget Department collates estimates and sends a Draft Estimate with an Executive Brief to the Governor; the State Estimates are discussed at the State Executive Council; the final Draft Budget goes to the House of Assembly for hearings and approval; the law is returned to the Governor for assent; the Commissioner for Finance then briefs the public
State Auditor-General approves the MDA estimates, the Public Account Committee passes the Appropriation Bill, and the Permanent Secretary gives assent
questions.explanation: This follows the order described on pages 28–29: collation and submission to the Governor, consideration by the State Executive Council, submission to the House of Assembly, legislative hearings and passage of the Appropriation Bill, return to the Governor for assent, and the public budget briefing by the Commissioner for Finance.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the meaning of Internal Audit in the seminar?
options: A continuous review of accounting, operational and internal control systems as a service to management
An annual examination of government revenue conducted exclusively by the House of Assembly
A periodic inspection of payment vouchers to determine the salary entitlements of public officers
An independent legislative investigation into the financial activities of Ministries and Departments
questions.explanation: The seminar defines Internal Audit as a continuous review of accounting, operational and internal control systems provided as a service to the management of an entity.

questions.question: What is the central management-oriented purpose of Internal Audit as described in the seminar?
options: To replace the Accounting Officer in approving every departmental expenditure
To evaluate accounting and corporate governance processes and assist management in achieving organisational objectives
To prepare the State Government's annual Appropriation Bill
To assume responsibility for the collection and custody of public revenue
questions.explanation: Internal Audit involves evaluating accounting and corporate governance processes as a service to management, helping an organisation improve its operations and achieve intended results.

questions.question: An internal auditor discovers errors in an entity's financial and operational processes during a review. Which responsibility directly corresponds to the seminar's stated objectives of Internal Audit?
options: Transferring responsibility for the errors to the State Auditor-General
Suspending the officers responsible before any further review
Identifying problems and errors and ensuring timely corrections
Replacing the accounting records with a new set of financial statements
questions.explanation: One objective of Internal Audit is to identify problems and errors and ensure timely corrections.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately distinguishes an internal audit review from an internal control system, as described in the seminar?
options: Internal audit is established exclusively by the legislature, while internal control is established by the State Auditor-General
Internal audit deals only with cash transactions, while internal control deals exclusively with procurement
Internal audit concerns revenue collection, while internal control concerns preparation of the Appropriation Bill
Internal audit continuously reviews systems and processes, while internal control is the system established by management to safeguard resources and promote orderly operations
questions.explanation: Internal Audit is a continuous review of accounting, operational and internal control systems. Internal Control is the system of control, financial or otherwise, established by management to safeguard assets, ensure reliable records, promote efficiency and encourage adherence to policies.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects the objectives of internal control under the seminar?
options: To determine the salaries of accounting officers and regulate their promotion
To safeguard assets, ensure accurate and reliable records, promote operational efficiency and encourage adherence to policies
To replace internal auditors with external auditors in every government establishment
To authorise expenditure beyond approved budgetary provisions where necessary
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies safeguarding assets, securing the accuracy and reliability of records, promoting operational efficiency and encouraging adherence to policies as the objectives of internal control.

questions.question: Which of the following is specifically identified as one of the mechanisms through which internal control can be exercised?
options: Annual budget briefing by the Commissioner for Finance
Issuance of call circulars by the Head of Budget Office
Vote Books
Appointment and confirmation of public officers
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies Vote Books, External Auditors, Annual Board of Surveys, Public Accounts Committee, Accountant-General's Inspectorate Department and Board of Enquiry among the mechanisms through which internal control can be exercised.

questions.question: An internal auditor reviews the operations of an MDA and identifies risks that could affect its performance. Which responsibility best reflects the auditor's role in this situation?
options: Approving the budgetary estimates of the MDA
Authorising the disbursement of funds to the MDA
Appointing officers responsible for the identified operational areas
Assessing operational risks, monitoring how they are managed and reporting risks that come to the auditor's attention
questions.explanation: The seminar states that internal auditors assess risks associated with relevant areas of operations, monitor how those risks are being managed and report risks that come to their attention during review exercises.

questions.question: An internal auditor examines whether a Ministry is implementing the applicable government policies and regulations. Which stated role is being performed?
options: Reviewing the implementation of government policies and regulations pertaining to the MDA
Authorising government expenditure on behalf of the Commissioner for Finance
Preparing the financial statements of the Ministry
Determining the statutory allocation payable to the Ministry
questions.explanation: Reviewing the implementation of government policies and regulations pertaining to the MDA is one of the specific roles assigned to internal auditors.

questions.question: An officer evaluates the performance of a government programme and identifies areas where resources could be used more economically and efficiently. Which responsibility does this represent?
options: Reviewing procurement committee membership
Preparing a supplementary expenditure warrant
Appraising performance effectiveness and identifying opportunities to improve economy, efficiency and effectiveness
Certifying the financial statements for presentation to the House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The seminar requires internal auditors to appraise the effectiveness of performance and identify opportunities to improve economy, efficiency and effectiveness.

questions.question: A payment voucher has been prepared and is awaiting payment. Which audit activity is specifically assigned to the internal auditor before the payment is made?
options: Post-payment audit
Annual financial statement audit
Procurement compliance review
Prepayment audit
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically assigns internal auditors the responsibility of carrying out prepayment audits on payment vouchers that have been checked and passed before payment.

questions.question: Within what period does the seminar require the internal auditor to complete the prepayment audit after receiving the relevant payment voucher?
options: Four days
Seven days
Fourteen days
Thirty days
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the prepayment audit should be completed within four days of receipt of the relevant payment voucher.

questions.question: Which public-sector reform is identified in the seminar as the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System?
options: GIFMIS
IPPIS
IPSAS
EFCC
questions.explanation: IPPIS stands for Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System and is listed among the reforms achieved for better service delivery.

questions.question: Which acronym represents the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System?
options: IPPIS
IPSAS
ICPC
GIFMIS
questions.explanation: GIFMIS stands for Government Integrated Financial Management Information System, one of the public-sector reforms identified in the seminar.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the contribution of the e-payment system listed among the public-sector reforms?
options: It reduces the risk associated with transactions involving large volumes of cash under the cashless policy
It replaces all government financial regulations with electronic approval procedures
It transfers the responsibility for auditing public accounts to commercial banks
It removes the requirement for payment vouchers in government transactions
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the e-payment system as reducing the risk of transactions involving large cash volumes under the cashless policy.

questions.question: Which pair of reforms is expressly listed together in the seminar?
options: IPPIS and the Oaths Act
International Public Sector Accounting Standards and the National Chart of Accounts
GIFMIS and the Finance (Control and Management) Act
EFCC and the Public Accounts Committee
questions.explanation: International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) and the National Chart of Accounts are listed together among the reforms in the public sector.

questions.question: Which combination correctly reflects the responsibilities attributed to the Fiscal Responsibility Board in the seminar?
options: Approving payment vouchers, preparing financial statements and conducting procurement evaluations
Collecting internally generated revenue and issuing expenditure warrants
Promoting the State's economic activities, instituting good standard practices, regulating MDA functions and developing a reporting system for all MDAs
Auditing every government bank account and approving the State's annual budget
questions.explanation: The seminar attributes these responsibilities to the Fiscal Responsibility Board: promoting the State's economic activities, instituting good standard practices, regulating MDA functions and developing a reporting system for all MDAs.

questions.question: According to the seminar, when did the Akwa Ibom State Government begin preparing its IPSAS Cash-Based Financial Statement?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that preparation of the State's IPSAS Cash-Based Financial Statement began in 2015.

questions.question: Which accounting basis does the seminar identify for the State's 2021 Financial Statement?
options: Cash-Based accounting
IPSAS Accrual-Based accounting
Modified Cash-Based accounting
Budgetary accounting only
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies the 2021 Financial Statement of the State as IPSAS Accrual-Based.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a benefit of IPSAS implementation?
options: Elimination of the need for financial reporting by government
Automatic prevention of every form of financial misconduct
Recognition and valuation of government assets and liabilities
Removal of the requirement for public-sector accountability
questions.explanation: Recognition and valuation of government assets and liabilities is one of the benefits of IPSAS identified in the seminar. Other benefits include strengthened reporting, transparency, accountability and comparability.

questions.question: Which statement best describes procurement in government as presented in the seminar?
options: The process through which government entities collect taxes and statutory allocations
The process of auditing public expenditure before funds are released
The administrative procedure for recruiting contractors into public service
The process by which government entities acquire goods, services and works using public funds under specific laws, regulations and guidelines
questions.explanation: The seminar defines government procurement as the process through which government entities acquire goods, services and works using public funds under specific laws, regulations and guidelines.

questions.question: A procuring entity wants to ensure that procurement activities do not encourage fraud, waste, corruption or local protectionism. Which approach best reflects the procurement principles described in the seminar?
options: Restricting information to selected bidders and avoiding competition
Making information readily available, ensuring transparency and accountability, promoting competition and achieving value for money
Awarding contracts primarily on the basis of familiarity with suppliers
Reducing procurement oversight to accelerate the award of contracts
questions.explanation: The seminar emphasises transparency, accountability, readily available information, efficiency, competition and value for money, while preventing fraud, waste, corruption and local protectionism.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the procurement procedure outlined in the seminar?
options: Contract management, needs assessment, contract award, bid solicitation and procurement planning
Bid evaluation, procurement planning, needs assessment, contract management and contract award
Needs assessment, procurement planning, solicitation of bids, evaluation of bids, contract award and contract management
Procurement planning, contract management, bid solicitation, needs assessment and contract evaluation
questions.explanation: The procurement stages are presented in this order: needs assessment, planning, solicitation of bids, evaluation of bids, contract awards and contract management.

questions.question: During procurement, technical and financial evaluation of bids has been completed. Which subsequent stage includes the Certified Board's approval of a No Objection (NoB), as described in the seminar?
options: Needs assessment
Procurement planning
Contract management
Contract award
questions.explanation: The seminar places the Certified Board's approval of a No Objection (NoB) under contract awards, which follows the evaluation of bids.

questions.question: A Ministry is constituting its Procurement Planning Committee. Which statement correctly describes the role of the Procurement Unit?
options: It serves as the Secretary of the Procurement Planning Committee
It appoints the Accounting Officer as Chairman
It independently approves the contract award and No Objection
It replaces the Financial Unit and Legal Unit in committee membership
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Procurement Unit of the MDA serves as the Secretary of the Procurement Planning Committee. The Accounting Officer—Permanent Secretary, Director-General or Chief Executive Officer—appoints the committee.

questions.question: Who is identified as producing the State's financial statements and presenting them to the State Auditor-General within three months after the end of the fiscal year?
options: The Commissioner for Finance
The State Auditor-General
The State Accountant-General
The Public Account Committee
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the State Accountant-General produces the financial statements and presents them to the State Auditor-General within three months after the end of the fiscal year.

questions.question: Which combination correctly identifies the four financial statements listed in the seminar?
options: Cash Book, Vote Book, Payment Voucher Register and Bank Reconciliation Statement
Statement of Financial Position, Statement of Financial Performance, Statement of Changes in Net Assets/Equity and Statement of Cash Flows
Statement of Revenue, Statement of Expenditure, Appropriation Bill and Development Fund Statement
Statement of Assets, Statement of Liabilities, Statement of Procurement and Statement of Audit Findings
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies four statements: Statement of Financial Position, Statement of Financial Performance, Statement of Changes in Net Assets/Equity and Statement of Cash Flows.

questions.question: Which items does the seminar say are published alongside the State's financial statements?
options: Explanatory notes and a Statement of Accounting Policies
Payment vouchers and cash books
Audit queries and procurement bids
Warrants and departmental Vote Books
questions.explanation: The seminar states that explanatory notes and a Statement of Accounting Policies are published alongside the financial statements.

questions.question: On receipt of the State Financial Statements, what is the stated aim of the State Auditor-General's audit?
options: To approve every expenditure item before the House of Assembly considers the budget
To certify that all revenue collectors have lodged every receipt within 48 hours
To determine whether every procurement contract was awarded to the lowest bidder
To provide reasonable assurance on whether the statements fairly present the State's financial position, results of operation and cash flows in conformity with extant rules
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the audit aims to provide reasonable assurance on whether the financial statements fairly present the State's financial position, results of operation and cash flows in conformity with extant rules.

questions.question: Within what period must the State Auditor-General submit the audit report to the State House of Assembly after receiving the Accountant-General's financial statements?
options: Within 90 days
Within 30 days
Within 60 days
Within 120 days
questions.explanation: The seminar requires the State Auditor-General to submit the report to the State House of Assembly within 90 days of receiving the financial statements from the Accountant-General.

questions.question: Which combination describes the contents of the Auditor-General's report as presented in the seminar?
options: Only the final audited balance sheet and the approved annual budget
A report on the financial statements, a summary of unresolved audit issues arising from audit inspection, and reports of special investigations
Only a list of officers queried and the proposed disciplinary sanctions
A procurement plan, a schedule of recurrent warrants and a cash book summary
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Auditor-General's report is made up of a report on the financial statement, a summary of unresolved audit issues arising from audit inspection, together with reports of special investigations.

questions.question: Which description correctly identifies the Public Account Committee of the State House of Assembly?
options: An administrative department within the Ministry of Finance
An independent audit institution established to replace the State Auditor-General
A statutory body established to examine the audited accounts of government and other statutory bodies
A procurement committee responsible for approving contracts
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Public Account Committee as a statutory body established to examine the audited accounts of government and other statutory bodies.

questions.question: Which action is specifically assigned to the Public Account Committee in relation to government officers queried in the Auditor-General's report?
options: Issue payment vouchers to the officers concerned
Approve their departments' budget estimates
Transfer them to the State Auditor-General's Office
Invite them to appear before the committee for questioning
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Public Account Committee invites government officers queried in the Auditor-General's report to appear before it for questioning.

questions.question: An officer has been queried in an audit report. Which additional requirement may the Public Account Committee impose on an affected officer under the seminar?
options: Produce documents to absolve the officer from the queries
Prepare a supplementary warrant for the expenditure
Approve the officer's next annual promotion
Transfer custody of the departmental Vote Book to the committee
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Public Account Committee requires affected officers to produce documents to absolve them from queries.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressly included among the Public Account Committee's examination responsibilities?
options: Issuing recurrent expenditure warrants to MDAs
Examining the audited reports and accounts of any public body
Preparing and signing the State's financial statements
Approving the appointment of Sub-Accounting Officers
questions.explanation: The seminar lists examination of the audited reports and accounts of any public body among the committee's functions.

questions.question: A government has an interest in a particular project. Which related examination is expressly listed as a function of the Public Account Committee?
options: Approving the project's original procurement plan
Issuing a Development Fund Warrant for the project
Examining the accounts of projects in which the government has an interest
Appointing the project's Accounting Officer
questions.explanation: The seminar assigns the Public Account Committee the function of examining the accounts of projects in which the government has an interest.

questions.question: A public body is suspected of incurring irregular expenditure and spending beyond its approved provision. Which Public Account Committee function is most directly relevant?
options: Preparing the affected body's next annual budget
Issuing a Virement Warrant to regularise the expenditure
Appointing an internal auditor to the body
Examining government expenditure where irregularities or over-expenditure have occurred
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly lists examination of government expenditure where irregularities or over-expenditure have occurred as a function of the Public Account Committee.

questions.question: After examining public accounts and identifying findings, through which channel does the Public Account Committee produce its report under the seminar?
options: Through the House of Assembly to the Executive
Directly to the Accountant-General for approval
Through the Commissioner for Finance to the Treasury
Directly to the affected MDA without reporting to the House
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Public Account Committee produces its report of findings through the House of Assembly to the Executive.

questions.question: Which oversight responsibility is also attributed to the Public Account Committee?
options: Issuing warrants to all Ministries and Departments
Carrying out oversight functions to Ministries, Departments and Agencies under its jurisdiction
Preparing all MDA financial statements
Conducting the day-to-day internal audit of every MDA
questions.explanation: The seminar lists oversight functions to Ministries, Departments and Agencies under the committee's jurisdiction among its major functions.

questions.question: Who is responsible for appointing the Procurement Planning Committee of a Ministry, Department or Agency, according to the seminar?
options: The State Auditor-General
The Commissioner for Finance
The Accounting Officer, namely the Permanent Secretary, Director-General or Chief Executive Officer
The Public Account Committee
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Accounting Officer—the Permanent Secretary, Director-General or Chief Executive Officer—shall appoint the Procurement Planning Committee.

questions.question: Who is identified as the Chairperson of the Procurement Planning Committee?
options: The representative of the Procurement Unit
The representative of the Financial Unit
The representative of the Legal Unit
The Permanent Secretary, Director-General or Chief Executive Officer, or a representative
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the Permanent Secretary, Director-General or Chief Executive Officer, or a representative, as Chairperson of the Procurement Planning Committee.

questions.question: A procuring MDA establishes its Procurement Planning Committee. Which unit should have a representative because it is directly within the MDA and in need of the procurement?
options: The unit directly within the MDA that is in need of the procurement
The State Auditor-General's Office
The Office of the Public Account Committee
The Revenue Collector's Unit
questions.explanation: The seminar includes a representative of the unit directly within the MDA that is in need of the procurement.

questions.question: Which financial function must be represented on the Procurement Planning Committee?
options: The office of the State Auditor-General
The Financial Unit of the procuring entity
The Office of the Accountant-General only
The State House of Assembly's Finance Committee
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Financial Unit of the procuring entity shall have a representative on the Procurement Planning Committee.

questions.question: Which department is expressly required to have a representative on the Procurement Planning Committee for its planning and research role?
options: The Internal Audit Unit
The Department of Establishments
The Planning, Research and Statistics Department
The State Auditor-General's Office
questions.explanation: The seminar specifies that the Planning, Research and Statistics (PRS) Department shall have a representative on the Procurement Planning Committee.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressly listed as a member of the Procurement Planning Committee?
options: The State Auditor-General
The Chairman of the Public Account Committee
The State Accountant-General in every case
The Legal Unit of the procuring entity
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Legal Unit of the procuring entity shall be a member of the Procurement Planning Committee.

questions.question: Which additional personnel category is expressly required to be represented on the Procurement Planning Committee?
options: Technical Personnel of the procuring entity
All Revenue Collectors in the MDA
Representatives of every contractor that submits a bid
All members of the State Executive Council
questions.explanation: The seminar includes Technical Personnel of the procuring entity as members of the Procurement Planning Committee.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a member or represented unit on the Procurement Planning Committee in the seminar?
options: The Financial Unit
The State Auditor-General's Office
The Legal Unit
The Planning, Research and Statistics Department
questions.explanation: The seminar lists the Financial Unit, Legal Unit and Planning, Research and Statistics Department among the committee's represented units. It does not identify the State Auditor-General's Office as a committee member.

questions.question: Which of the following is specifically identified as the work covered by contract management in the procurement procedure?
options: Needs assessment and preparation of the procurement plan only
Solicitation of bids and technical/financial evaluation only
Execution, performance monitoring, payment and dispute resolution
Issuance of call circulars and presentation of the State budget
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies contract management as covering execution, performance monitoring, payment and dispute resolution.

questions.question: Which report does the seminar specifically identify among the Public Account Committee's functions to examine in relation to local government?
options: The annual procurement plan of each Local Government
The State budget briefing delivered by the Commissioner for Finance
The payment voucher schedule prepared by the Accountant-General
The reports of the State Auditor-General for Local Government
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically lists examination of the reports of the State Auditor-General for Local Government among the Public Account Committee's functions.
